answer.A: Give priority to investing in all first-tier cities (such as Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen) because these cities have developed economies and dense populations, which can naturally reduce the vacancy risk and improve the investment return.
answer.B: Give priority to investing in first-tier cities with low vacancy rates in core business districts and pay attention to cities with outstanding net absorption volume performance. answer.F: In second-tier cities with high vacancy rates, reduce investment in new development projects and instead attract tenants from high-demand industries (such as technology or finance) to revitalize the existing stock because these industries have the highest leasing demand share and can quickly improve the vacancy situation.
answer.G: In cities where there is a significant difference in the vacancy rate between the core business district and the whole city, focus on investing in the core area rather than the whole city scope because the vacancy rate in the core business district is generally lower and more resilient, which can ensure a more stable cash flow.
